transport: Two separate radios' worth of behaviour on one device, and only one of them is reachable by a third party. (1) VE.Smart Networking — 'a wireless technology based on Bluetooth Smart' (Smart Battery Sense Manual rev 02, §1), the path by which it feeds voltage and temperature to Victron MPPTs. Encrypted, proprietary, no published record format; not readable by anything that is not a Victron charger.
blocks: Asserted, not proven: extra-manufacturer-data record type 0x02 'Battery Monitor', whose layout IS in the committed vendor PDF — battery voltage 16 bits at 0.01 V, an aux-input union selected by a 2-bit `aux_input_type` where value 2 means VE_REG_BAT_TEMPERATURE at 0.01 K. What no vendor document states is that a Smart Battery Sense emits record 0x02. That link comes from one implementation only.

Low-temperature and high-temperature alarms live in there, which is the one thing a Quebec cabin most wants from a battery temperature sensor, and there is no MetricKind for an alarm bitfield or for any single alarm bit., Stored trends: roughly 181 days of history at 30-minute resolution held in the device's non-volatile memory (VictronConnect app manual rev 22 §11.1 — the Smart Battery Sense's store is far longer than the ~46 days of other products). Same finding docs/catalog/ve-direct.md already reached about MPPT day records: this is a different contract shape, not a missing MetricKind., Whether the device is currently contributing to a VE.Smart network. The manual's LED table treats 'measuring but not joined' and 'measuring and contributing' as distinct states. Nothing in the contract can say a sensor is measuring correctly but its data is going nowhere.
